extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and NIH/NIAID grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Standard operating procedure describing the NIH/NIAID criteria reviewers should use to evaluate research grant applications, including the five core review criteria, additional topic-specific review items, and the new Simplified Peer Review Framework effective Jan 25, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers give applications an overall impact score after considering the review criteria. An overall impact score reflects their assessment of the project’s likelihood to exert a sustained, powerful influence on its field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact is derived from consideration of the core criteria and additional items; reviewers should judge likelihood of sustained, powerful influence. Investigator-initiated R01s typically use standard criteria; other application types may add criteria that should be incorporated into the core criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? Is the prior research that serves as the key support for the proposed project rigorous? If the aims of the project are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how successful completion will change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventive interventions that drive the field. Assess rigor of the prior supporting research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PDs/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If early-stage investigators, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects, evaluate whether investigators have complementary and integrated expertise, and whether leadership approach, governance, and organizational structure are appropriate for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether concepts/approaches/instrumentation/interventions are novel to one field or broadly novel, or whether a refinement, improvement, or new application is proposed. Assess degree of innovation relative to field norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the Specific Aims? Have plans been included to address weaknesses in the rigor of prior research that serves as key support?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate strategies to ensure a robust and unbiased approach; whether potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success are presented; feasibility for early-stage projects and plans to manage particularly risky aspects. Assess plans to address relevant biological variables (e.g., sex) for vertebrate animal or human studies. For human subjects/clinical research, see additional protections and inclusion questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources adequate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the project will benefit from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: For most research grants and mentored career development awards, reviewers should assess the project's rigor and transparency as addressed by questions in the Significance and Approach sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For institutional training grants and career development awards, applicants are required to include formal instruction plans in rigorous experimental design and transparency to enhance reproducibility; see NIH guidance 'Enhancing Reproducibility Through Rigor and Transparency' for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified Peer Review Framework (post-Jan 25, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will use a Simplified Peer Review Framework for most research project grant applications, reorganizing the five regulatory criteria into three factors: Importance of the Research, Rigor and Feasibility, and Expertise and Resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications due on/after Jan 25, 2025, reviewers should apply the new framework; initiative-specific criteria still must be incorporated into these factors. Consult NIAID/NIH instructions for mapping traditional criteria into the simplified factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for human subjects (non-exempt)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving non-exempt human subjects, evaluate justification for involvement of human subjects and proposed protections from research risks according to five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess protections in the context of the scientific aims; consult SF 424 Application Guides and Guidelines for Reviewers: Protections for Human Subjects Criterion for detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for human subjects (exempt research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that meets the criteria for one or more exemption categories under 45 CFR Part 46, evaluate: (1) the justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ensure the exemption is justified and that subject involvement/characteristics and materials sources are appropriate; consult SF 424 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women, minorities, and individuals across the lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, assess adequacy of plans to include (or exclude) individuals on the basis of sex, race, and ethnicity and inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals of all ages as appropriate for the scientific goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also evaluate recruitment and retention plans. Note NIH changed definition of 'child' from under 21 to under 18 years of age. See SF 424 Application Guides and Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to: (1) description of proposed procedures (species, strains, ages, sex, total number), (2) justifications for use of animals versus alternatives and appropriateness of species, (3) interventions to minimize discomfort/distress/pain/injury (including use of analgesics/anesthetics/restraints), and (4) justification for euthanasia method if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If euthanasia method differs from AVMA guidelines, scientific justification must be described on the Cover Page Supplement form. See SF 424 guides and Worksheet for Applications Involving Animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment and whether adequate protection is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if proposed biosafety measures are sufficient; flag concerns that might jeopardize personnel or environmental safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a resubmission, evaluate the application as now presented while taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and the changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether previous weaknesses were adequately addressed and whether revisions improved the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a renewal application, consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate accomplishments, productivity, and whether the proposed renewal builds logically on prior progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision (supplement) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a revision, consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project. If the revision relates to investigation in the original application that was not recommended for approval, consider whether responses to prior reviewer comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are evident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the expansion is justified and whether prior concerns have been meaningfully addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative-specific / additional review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Some RFAs, PARs, and other initiatives may include additional review criteria; these should be incorporated into the five core criteria so they can be captured in the Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officers and scientific review officers should develop additional criteria only when necessary. Note: additional criteria cannot be recorded separately in the Commons; for standard program announcements you cannot include or expand additional review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR-specific review considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR and STTR applications may include additional review criteria (e.g., for Fast Track and Phase II applications) as specified in the SF 424 Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and applicants should consult the SBIR/STTR SF 424 Application Guide for Fast Track and Phase II-specific review requirements and criteria.
